title: Aligning company hypotheses to deliverables and cross-team commitments
creator: Priya Iyer
description:
Problem: Leadership-level hypotheses about next-quarter growth levers (routing policies, Dedicated adoption, Optimize recommendations) are not consistently mapped to concrete engineering deliverables and owner commitments. That gap causes missed milestones and unclear escalation paths when dependencies slip.

Objective: Produce a lightweight, repeatable playbook and a canonical artifacts bundle that maps each company-level hypothesis/OKR to: (a) measurable signal(s), (b) a set of initiatives and owner(s), (c) required dependencies across Eng/Design/Infra/Sales, and (d) escalation rules and timeboxed contingency actions.

Scope: Company-level OKRs for FY2026 Q2 planning, plus three supporting initiatives per OKR. Includes templates for initiative charters, a dependency register, and a one-page decision ledger for exec reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical mapping doc exists in Confluence with one row per OKR hypothesis and linked initiative charters
Initiative charters created and owned by specific PM/Eng/Design leads with estimates and risk rating
Dependency register populated and prioritized with owners and RTT (required-to-resolve) windows
Escalation ladder documented and validated by GTM and Infra leads
Dashboard widgets created in Console to show progress signals (latency, cost/unit, adoption metrics) for each hypothesis
next_steps: Run kickoff workshop w/ exec sponsors, ENG leads, Design leads (2026-03-12) — invite: @eng-leads, @design-leads, @sales-leads
Draft Confluence template and initiative charter by 2026-03-18 (owner: Liam)
Collect initial dependency commitments and fill register by 2026-03-25
Sync with Reliability (ENG) to define SLO signals used in evaluation by 2026-03-29
Schedule 30m exec review for contingency decision-making week of 2026-04-06
risks_and_tradeoffs: Over-broad charters: risk of ownership ambiguity vs. overly prescriptive charters that block team autonomy
Signal selection: picking noisy metrics could cause false positives; prefer stable leading indicators where possible
Resource contention: multiple initiatives targeting the same infra optimizations could require prioritization or conserved capacity
